answer: Running 116 aliases therefore means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest participants do not face at scale. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the copper schedule in the knoll ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the zephyr checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 5 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. That is 5 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
